subject: Workplace Skills
title: Goals Set Direction, Systems Get Results
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Goals Set Direction, Systems Get Results.

hook.text: Every Olympic sprinter has the same goal: win gold. The difference is in their training systems.

buildup.text: Goals tell you where to go. Systems tell you how to get there. Without systems, goals are just wishes.

discovery.text: James Clear argues you don't rise to your goals; you fall to the level of your systems every time.

twist.text: Goal-focused people celebrate once and lose motivation. System-focused people improve continuously.

climax.text: Set the goal once for direction. Then spend all your energy designing and refining the daily system.

punchline.text: Goals inspire. Systems deliver. Build the system.

quiz.question: Why are systems more important than goals according to James Clear?
options: Goals create unnecessary pressure and anxiety
You fall to the level of your systems, not your goals
Systems are easier to explain to others
